title: Johnny St. Cyr encourages him on the bench
summary: As a boy he kept time with sticks on a bench beside Johnny St. Cyr's combo, and St. Cyr told him to keep at it. St. Cyr later went to Chicago.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Yeah. I think it was a 28. And well I never did actually let me set in because I was kind of leery about setting in and you know in anybody's band or anything like that. So while we was living in Calton, Johnny Saint Seale was living up there at that time, well he used to play a little combo right at the corner from his house at Boydette and Hickory. He was living on Hickory between Boydette and Adams. Well he used to play there and he didn't have no drums handed so they had long benches and I used to have a pair of drumsticks and I used to sit on the side of the bench you know and pat my foot along with them keeping the tempo and beating on the bench you know. So he told me, he said, well you keep it up. He said, you'll probably get somewhere if you're really interested in it. Well after we moved back downtown and I started and I got my first set of drums, well he went to Chicago. When he went to play with Louie, I'm more sure he left to go play with Louie at that time, the first time he went to Chicago. Yeah. And after he left Louie he went with Professor Cook. I'm more sure that's the way it was, but I know that first was playing out here on the steam of Capitol.
Yes, he played with Faith Marable. Yeah, that's right, yeah, Faith Marable, yeah.
